businessModel: Regional 3PL (third-party logistics) provider with transportation and warehousing
sourceNote: Real-world case from logistics sector. Business context reflects typical regional 3PL facing margin pressure from e-commerce disruption.

ownerIntake.businessType: Third-party logistics provider serving retail, CPG, and e-commerce customers. 28 warehouses across Southeast US, 400 employees, $92M annual revenue. EBITDA margin 12% ($11M), down from 14% (three years ago). Profit pressure from e-commerce customer growth (higher operational complexity, lower margins vs. traditional retail) and rising labor costs.
ownerIntake.stage: Mature profitable: EBITDA $11M (12% margin), operating cash flow strong $9M, return on assets 6.3% (below peer median 8%). Customer concentration risk: top 3 customers = 28% of revenue. Margin compression driven by (1) shift to e-commerce customers (lower margins), (2) labor inflation (+12% in 24 months), (3) automation capex requirements.
ownerIntake.ownerGoal: Return EBITDA to 15%+ margin within 24 months through operational efficiency and customer mix optimization.
ownerConstraints: Labor market: Warehouse staffing tight; wages +12% in 24 months. Automation capex required to reduce labor dependency, but ROI uncertain.

Customer mix shift: E-commerce customers (38% of revenue) require higher service complexity (faster fulfillment, returns handling) at lower margins (8-10% vs. retail 15-18%). Traditional retail shrinking.
Automation capex: Modern 3PL requires significant capex (robotics, WMS upgrades). Estimated $8-12M to upgrade 28 warehouses. Current cash flow cannot support full modernization.
Competitive dynamics: Amazon Logistics, national 3PLs entering regional markets, competing on price and technology. Regional 3PLs consolidating. Scale matters for profitability.
Economic sensitivity: Retail/e-commerce volume sensitive to economic cycles; FY2025 e-commerce growth 8% (vs. 15% historical average).
ownerIntake.immediateConcern: EBITDA margin eroding (14% → 12% in 3 years) while revenue growing slowly (5% YoY current vs. 12% three years ago). Growth slowing and margins compressing = profitability squeeze. Net income declining despite revenue growth. Must determine whether problem is structural (customer mix shift to lower-margin e-commerce) or operational (labor cost inflation, underutilized capacity).

clientContext.revenueImpactUrgency: CRITICAL (margin erosion and growth slowdown threaten exit valuation)

businessProblem: A regional 3PL provider is experiencing simultaneous margin compression (14% → 12% EBITDA in three years) and growth slowdown (12% growth three years ago → 5% YoY current) driven by a shift in customer mix toward lower-margin e-commerce business while labor costs inflate (+12% in 24 months). Management must determine whether the margin decline is permanent (structural shift to lower-margin e-commerce business model) or temporary (operational inefficiency, underutilization, labor cost inflation), and identify which levers (pricing, service model, customer mix, automation, consolidation) can restore 15% EBITDA margin within 24 months.

evidence.finding: EBITDA margin eroding (14% 3 years ago → 12% current), 200bps decline. Revenue growing slowly (5% YoY) compared to historical growth (12% three years ago). Net income declining despite revenue growth, indicating margin deterioration outpacing revenue growth. Operating cash flow still positive ($9M), but declining as % of revenue.
evidence.source: P&L trend, margin analysis, cash flow statements

evidence.finding: E-commerce customer growth driving mix shift: e-commerce now 38% of revenue (growing faster) but at lower margins (8-10% vs. retail 15-18%). Traditional retail declining but higher-margin. This is structural shift: e-commerce is growing industry-wide and customers are shifting, but it erodes 3PL margins due to operational complexity (returns, speed requirements) without price premium.
evidence.source: Customer segment analysis, revenue mix tracking, margin by segment

evidence.finding: Labor costs rising +12% in 24 months while utilization only 72%, suggesting excess capacity. Automation gap vs. competitors; modern 3PLs using robotics/WMS, but this company is still labor-intensive. Capex requirements ($8-12M for full automation) exceed annual cash flow generation ($9M), creating modernization constraint.
evidence.source: Labor cost trends, capacity analysis, competitive benchmarking
